title: Where is the angle in an animal's open mouth?
description: A snake, a fish, a bird and a crocodile open their mouths by different amounts. The two jaws are marked as the arms and the hinge as the vertex, and the mouths are lined up from the least open to the widest. Keeko's doubt is that the biggest animal must have the biggest angle.
teaching_notes: One idea: the two jaws are the arms, the hinge is the vertex, and more turn between the jaws gives a larger angle. Watch for students who think a bigger animal always makes a bigger angle.

source: Look at these animals opening their mouths (snake, fish, bir
video_script.why: The child sees an angle in an open mouth and orders angles by how wide the mouths open.
video_script.substitution: the book's own picture of a snake, a fish, a bird and a crocodile with their mouths open
video_script.anchor: the four animals of the book with their mouths open by different amounts
video_script.wrong_answer: the biggest animal has the biggest angle
video_script.wrong_move: judges the angle by the size of the animal instead of the turn of the jaws
video_script.payoff_line: The wider the mouth is open, the greater the angle

final_answer.value: yes; jaws are the arms, hinge is the vertex; crocodile's is widest
final_answer.spoken: yes, the jaws are the arms and the hinge is the vertex, and the crocodile's mouth looks widest

maths_rules: each mouth: the upper jaw and the lower jaw are the two arms; the place where the jaws join is the vertex
the more the jaws turn apart, the greater the angle
by the book's picture, the crocodile's mouth is open the widest, so its angle looks the greatest
order the four angles by how wide each mouth is open, from the least open to the widest
the order is read from the picture, so it is about, not exact
slip: the size of the animal does not decide the size of the angle
video_script.design: One idea: a mouth is an angle, and a wider opening means a greater angle. The four animals of the book stay on the board all video. Keeko's doubt: a bigger animal means a bigger angle.
open_questions: The order of the four mouths is read from the book's picture, which could not be viewed; only the crocodile being widest is taken from the worklist.

narration: <bookmark mark='arms'/>The two rays that make an angle are called its arms.
<bookmark mark='vertex'/>The point where the arms meet is called the vertex.
<bookmark mark='turn'/>The more the arms turn apart, the larger the angle.

narration: <bookmark mark='order'/>Step three, compare the turn. The more the jaws turn apart, the larger the angle. Line up the mouths from the least open to the widest.

beats.on_screen: Answer: each mouth makes an angle; in the picture the crocodile widest
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The wider the mouth is open, the greater the angle.
Yes, every mouth makes an angle. In the picture, the crocodile's mouth is open the widest.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the biggest animal has the biggest angle.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But the angle is the turn of the jaws, not the size of the animal.
<bookmark mark='small'/>A big animal that opens a little makes a smaller angle than a small animal that opens wide.
